ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: ideoligions and the council
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: How colonists are drawn to the other ideoligions around them, ideoligion evenings, a wavering colonist's wish to learn another ideoligion, the question when ideoligions clash, and the decree that names one ideoligion the colony's.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Pick the speaker's evening for when the open-minded and the wavering are at home: they are the ones it can move.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
With Ideology, each colonist holds their ideoligion with a certainty from 0 to 100%. Under 60% they are wavering, from 85% devout; at none left, the game converts them to the ideoligion that wore it down. Beside it, Rimfolk keeps how strongly each colonist is drawn to each other ideoligion around them, their leanings, shown under their certainty on the Culture tab. When a leaning passes their certainty, they take that ideoligion up. A conversion is always the game's own, with a message and a line in the chronicle.
The council has four ways to work with the colony's ideoligions: an ideoligion evening it can call, a wish a wavering colonist may make, a question that comes when ideoligions clash, and a decree that names one ideoligion the colony's. Their costs are trust and certainty, never a bad mood. None of it happens without Ideology, in classic mode, or with "Ideoligions in the colony" off in the settings.

li.heading: Leanings
li.text: Once a day each leaning fades a little and is fed by what draws them. The strongest wears on their certainty, against the game's own daily recovery, which gives a content colonist about three points a day and an unhappy one less. When a growing leaning passes their certainty by 5 points (and is at least 30%), they take that ideoligion up, as firmly as they had leaned, and settle into it for a year: meanwhile no leaning wears on them or takes over. The one they leave stays with them as a small leaning (at most 10%), so they may drift back if it grows again; someone with dear friends on both sides may change once in a long while, never back and forth. A leaning passing 50% is told once, and an ideoligion the game has let go of (its last believers gone) is forgotten.

table.li: What | Each day

Its believers in the colony | Up to 4%, more the more there are and the closer they are: a rival adds nothing, a stranger half, a friend a whole, the dearest one and a half, a lover or family half again
The decree naming it | 4% more (half for someone whose ideoligion frowns on being preached to)
How open they are | The closed-minded take 40% of it, the open up to 160%
Fading | 3% of the leaning, so a lone believer barely matters and a whole colony does
Wear on certainty | 12% of the strongest leaning (70% of that while they're devout)

li.after: A talk, an evening, a crisis or a council answer that sways someone toward an ideoligion feeds their leaning toward it by as much. For a content colonist of average openness: with the decree and friends among its believers, about 25 days; with the decree alone, about 35; four friends of another ideoligion and no decree, about 70; a lone believer of a minority never pulls the others over. The open come round sooner, the closed-minded later, the unhappy sooner.

li.heading: An ideoligion evening
li.text:
A gathering where one ideoligion is spoken for, between five and eleven in the evening, for about two hours. The speaker is the ideoligion's moral guide if they're at home, else its most devout believer with the best Social skill. It is held at the ideoligion's own altar or ideogram if one is built (one in its style, or for the colony's own ideoligion any that isn't another ideoligion's), else round a fire, at the dining table or a gather spot. It needs "Answers play out on the map" on.
The colony can hold one every five days at most, and the same ideoligion one every ten. It can be called from a day on the calendar kept as an ideoligion evening (whatever the gap since the last), by answering yes when one of the devout asks the council for one, or from the ideoligions page. When nobody but the speaker means to come, there is no evening, and that ideoligion can't ask again for ten days.

table.li: Who | Comes
Believers of the speaker's ideoligion | Always
Someone whose ideoligion frowns on being preached to | Never: they stay away and say so
Anyone else | 35% to start with; up to 50% more or less by openness, and the same by their opinion of the speaker; 25% more if wavering, 15% less if devout; never under 5% or over 95%

li.heading: How it goes
li.text: When it's over the evening is judged from 0 to 1: the speaker's Social skill counts most (up to 0.55 at 20), their warmth up to 0.15 either way, how many came to listen up to 0.2 (six or more), and the ideoligion's own altar 0.1. Broken off early, it counts half; without the speaker there, it counts nothing. The speaker gets a little Social practice (250) however it goes.

table.li: Evening | Score | Listeners of other ideoligions | Believers who came | Everyone who came
Poor | under 0.3 | Nothing | Nothing | Nothing but a line
Good | 0.3 to 0.65 | Swayed toward the ideoligion, 6% to 9% to start with | 3.2% to 4.6% surer | Recreation (12% of the bar) and fellowship, no mood
Fine | 0.65 or more | Swayed, 9% to 12% to start with | 4.6% to 6% surer | +3 mood for a day and a half, through the shared good-mood budget

li.after: A listener's own side counts on top: the open-minded are moved up to half again as much and the closed half as much, the proud give less ground, a friend of the speaker is heard and a rival less, and the speaker's conversion power counts. No single moment takes more than 15%. Believers are steadied half again as much with a chaplain at home. Those of other ideoligions who listened remember the evening with the speaker.

li.heading: A wavering colonist's wish
li.text: Someone wavering (under 60%) who thinks well of a devout believer of another ideoligion (opinion 20 or more) may ask for an evening learning about that ideoligion; never someone whose own ideoligion frowns on being preached to. Promised, the evening is arranged: they walk over to the believer that evening and keep them company for a couple of hours (with answers not playing out on the map, the next time the two are together). Going to an evening of that ideoligion also counts. Granted, they are swayed toward the ideoligion (12% to start with, through the same sides as above, unless an ideoligion evening already did it), +3 mood for 3 days, and the two share the memory. Ignored, it lapses after 8 days at a wish's usual cost.

li.heading: When ideoligions clash
li.text: A council question for a colony of two or more ideoligions with at least two believers each, or one split half or more of the way (six people of five ideoligions are). It comes half as often in a quiet colony as after a quarrel between believers of different ideoligions in the last five days, or while an ideoligion's altar stands, and at most once in 30 days. A is a believer of the largest ideoligion, B one of another.

table.li: Answer | Trust | Certainty | On the map
Share the altar: the ideoligions take turns | +2 for the open-minded, -1 for the devout | Nothing | The ideoligions at the altar (or the fire) together
A corner for each ideoligion (if unanswered) | +1 for everyone with an ideoligion | Everyone 3% surer of their own | A letter suggests a corner for each, and a few clear them

Name the largest ideoligion the colony's | +3 for its believers; -2 for everyone else, and -4 more for the devout of other ideoligions who take it hard (60%, 90% if their ideoligion frowns on preaching) | Everyone else swayed 3% toward it | Its speaker says a word for it to the colony

li.heading: An ideoligion evening, asked for
li.text: Now and then one of the devout who would speak for their ideoligion asks the council for an evening of it (at most once in 20 days, only when one could be held). Holding it, open to all, calls it at once and earns the asker 2 trust. An evening for the ideoligion's own believers only gathers them at its altar or a fire, makes them 4% surer, and earns 1 trust (it needs two of them at home). Not now (if unanswered) costs the asker 2 trust.

li.heading: One ideoligion for the colony (a decree)
li.text: You choose the ideoligion as you declare it, the largest first. It holds for 15 days, with 20 days to wait before it can be declared again (the decrees page's fatigue and forcing apply as for any decree). It has no mood of its own. Lifting it ends all of it at once, and it is never listed with only one ideoligion at home.

table.li: While it holds | Each day
Colonists of other ideoligions | Lean toward it 4% more (see Leanings above), whatever their certainty
Colonists of other ideoligions | Lose trust: 0.25 if open-minded, 0.5 most, 0.75 if devout, 1 if their ideoligion frowns on being preached to
Its believers | Speak of it half again as often; every council meeting opens with a word from one of them

li.after: Its devout believers love it and the rest of them like it; the devout of other ideoligions hate it and will petition to lift it, the curious don't mind, and the rest dislike it.
